messages:
Leah W: Heads-up — multiple customers reported a recent jump in p95/p99 on text-gen endpoints after the weekend deploy. Noticing long tails that look correlated with continuous-batcher configs we rolled (timeout -> 8ms, max_batch_tokens -> 4096).
Omar K: seeing the same. Graphs from prometheus show p50 stable but p99 doubled for a subset of requests. Happens across two regions but more pronounced in us-east-1.
Maria S: any correlation with model variants or quantized kernels?
Leah W: started by looking at routing logs: traffic routed to the same model variant. No kernel switch. The only infra change was the batcher defaults we pushed Friday night.
Evan P: can you paste the exact config that was deployed?
Leah W: sure — from infra-rollout: 
```
continuous_batcher: 
  enabled: true
  batch_timeout_ms: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  prefer_latency: false
```
Omar K: 8ms is pretty aggressive. For small, bursty requests that prevents batching and increases cold-starts of the KV cache plus queuing spikes. p99 will suffer if some requests miss the prefix cache.
support-bot: alert: ticket #3421 (AcmeCorp) — elevated latency (p99 2.1s) on /v1/generate. Customer impact: degraded UX.
Maria S: I reproduced locally with the load generator using mix of short prompts and saw similar tail when timeout <= 10ms. If I increase to 25ms, p99 drops back down but p50 slightly increases. Tradeoff.
Leah W: can we get a quick mitigation for the impacted customers while we investigate root cause?
Omar K: short-term: roll back batch_timeout_ms to previous 25ms for hosted-api fleet. We can do a staged rollout for us-east-1 only. That should reduce the tail.
Evan P: +1. Also add a temporary per-customer override to avoid penalizing customers with high request burstiness.
sre-bot: deployment lock removed: rolling update allowed.
Leah W: plan: 1) rollback timeout to 25ms in us-east-1 (owner: Omar) 2) run targeted load test with current and previous config (owner: Maria) 3) dig into batching telemetry to see which request shapes cause misses (owner: Evan) 4) follow-up with product/support for communication (owner: Leah).
Omar K: starting rollback now. Command: 
```
infractl apply --env=prod --region=us-east-1 --set continuous_batcher.batch_timeout_ms=25 
```
Maria S: running load test against a canary with both configs, will attach histograms. Test script: small_prompts_mix.py (200rps, 50% short <= 40 tokens, 50% medium). Repro steps: curl to /_internal/debug/batcher-stats to capture per-request batching decision.
Leah W: paste sample output from debug endpoint when you have it.
Maria S: sample from canary (timeout=8ms): 
```
batch_decisions: [
  {req_id: a1, batch_size:1, wait_ms:2, kv_cache_hit:false},
  {req_id: a2, batch_size:5, wait_ms:8, kv_cache_hit:true},
  {req_id: a3, batch_size:1, wait_ms:1, kv_cache_hit:false},
  {req_id: a4, batch_size:10, wait_ms:8, kv_cache_hit:false},
]
observed_p99: 2100ms
```
Maria S: with timeout=25ms: 
```
batch_decisions: [
  {req_id: b1, batch_size:6, wait_ms:20, kv_cache_hit:true},
  {req_id: b2, batch_size:7, wait_ms:22, kv_cache_hit:true},
]
observed_p99: 400ms
```
Omar K: important signal: kv_cache_hit correlates strongly with latency. When small bursts bypass batching we get cache misses and large decoding cost.
Evan P: longer term we should consider adaptive timeouts per route: e.g., increase timeout for short-prompt-heavy routes or add a tiny per-customer adaptive controller that raises timeout when bursty pattern detected. Also consider opportunistic early-merge: wait up to Nms but if queue length > X, flush.
Leah W: agree. For now, rollback should buy us time. Maria, once you have histograms, open a tracking ticket with traces and request IDs so we can link to customer logs.
Maria S: uploaded histograms + sample traces to the incident doc. p99 heatmap shows tail concentrated on requests with prompt length <= 20 tokens.
Omar K: rolled back in us-east-1 canary. Monitoring: initial signs p99 dropping. I'll extend to the rest of the region after 15m if stable.
support-bot: ticket #3421 update: we rolled internal config, ask customer to verify.
Leah W: follow-ups: - schedule a postmortem with product and devex (include customer repro steps) - add a telemetry metric for 'batch_timeout_ms' per request so regressions get detected earlier - prototype adaptive timeout controller
Evan P: also add a Canary for batching config changes to block straight-to-global pushes. Maybe gate via traffic-weight threshold + synthetic short-prompt load.
Leah W: thanks all. Quick notes for the postmortem: root cause = overly aggressive continuous-batcher timeout (8ms) that caused small-burst requests to miss batching and KV cache, increasing p99; mitigation = rollback to 25ms + per-customer overrides; next actions include adaptive timeouts and better canarying.
Omar K: +:thumbsup: Will update the change log and follow up with on-call if anything flips.
Evan P: I'll draft the design doc for adaptive timeouts this afternoon.
Leah W: closing thread for now; reopen if p99 doesn't stabilize. :white_check_mark:
